# odyssey-034 review (Odyssey 8.97–194)

Reviewer: adversarial, two passes. `t` untouched in every unit (checked by comparing all 59 `t` before and after). Neighbour checked: odyssey-033's last unit (8.94–96) closes on "αἶψα δὲ Φαιήκεσσι φιληρέτμοισι μετηύδα" with Alcinous the speaker, so the speech opening at 8.97 is right and unit 97 takes `p` and `mark`. No scansion flags in the packet, so no hand scans were required and no metrical sentence was added. No modern translation was opened or recalled; the renderings that arrive readily were rebuilt from the case relations (see refused list).

Severity: high = wrong sense or wrong text; medium = a false grammatical label, false cross-reference, wrong quotation mark, or l/i disagreement in force; minor = wording, precision, consistency.

Totals: high 0, medium 14, minor 20 (34 changes).

## Pass 1 — units.json

| line · field | sev | what was wrong | what done |
|---|---|---|---|
| 178 · l, i | medium | Stray opening “ on the unit at 178. Odysseus's speech opens at 166 (mark 'Odysseus speaks again') and runs unbroken to the ” at 185; no ” closes it before 178, and 178 carries no `mark`. | Removed the “ from `l` and `i`. |
| 97 · n | medium | "The same line begins Alcinous' speeches at 7.136, 7.186 and 8.26." 7.136 in odyssey-031 is narration (εὗρε δὲ Φαιήκων ἡγήτορας ἠδὲ μέδοντας, accusative), not this line. | Now "at 7.186 and 8.26". |
| 107 · n | medium | "'went' … supplied from ἦρχε": the others are not leading, so the verb is not ἦρχε. | "supplied from the sense". |
| 109 · n | medium | ἕσπετο called "again unaugmented". It is the augmented aorist of ἕπομαι (ἐ + σπ- → ἑσπ-). | Rewritten: augment run together with the stem σπ-. |
| 133 · n | medium | ἐρώμεθα called "a hortative subjunctive with the short vowel"; the vowel is ω, the long-vowel form. | Now "aorist subjunctive of ἔρομαι, aorist ἠρόμην" (accent is recessive, which is the aorist's). |
| 186 · i | medium | "a discus larger and thicker": πάχετον is the positive 'thick' (as `l` and the note have it), not a comparative. | "larger and thick". |
| 193 · n | medium | "Athena arrives without warning, in disguise": she has been in the story since 8.7 (odyssey-033), so 'without warning' is false to the reader. | Now: not named in this part until now, present in the likeness of a man. |
| 98 · n | minor | "the house rendering is 'the equal feast'": there is no table row; it is a new rendering of this part. | "the rendering used for it here". |

| 111 · n | minor | "The genitives υἱὸς Πολυνήου Τεκτονίδαο": υἱός is nominative. | Reworded: Πολυνήου genitive, Τεκτονίδαο patronymic. |
| 141 · n | minor | ἔειπες "with a lengthened stem": it is the augment before a stem that began with a digamma. | Reworded. |
| 142 · n | minor | "The object of both verbs, unstated, is the stranger": πέφραδε has the object μῦθον. | The stranger is the object of προκάλεσσαι and the one to whom the word is declared. |

| 186 · n | minor | "Φαίηκες is the spelling here, where Φαιήκων at 8.97 had the ι": both spellings have the ι; only the accent differs. | Now describes the accent (αί here, ή at 8.97). |
| 179 · n | minor | μυθεῖαι "is μυθέαι, the uncontracted second person middle"; that clashed with the glossary parse and is loose. | "the epic second person singular middle of μυθέομαι (Attic μυθῇ)". |

Checked and left: every other parse of the 170 novel forms, including the augment claims (βόμβησεν, ἔξαγεν, νείκεσε, πειρήσαντο, ἐπειρήσαντο, ὤρινας, ἐπώτρυνας), the elisions, the proper names, and the 8 other broadenings (αὐτὴν, αὐτῷ, καλὸν, μετὰ, πεδίοιο, τῇ, ἐπέτοντο, ἤ, ὑπὸ, ἄμφω). Length under 230, typographic ’ only, no "here", no line numbers. The 309 known forms were read against the lines; the gaps are the four broadenings added above.

The other rows were checked against the units' `l` and `i` and match (8.98, 8.115, 8.130/143, 8.132, 8.158, 8.165, ἥβη, ἀθλητήρ, the names). The 8.158 and 8.165 rows are consistent with the published 7.298 and 8.152 patterns.

## Findings considered and refused

- 98 `i` "the companion of the abundant feast" against `l` "a companion": English idiom, no difference in force.
- 161 `i` "the wares he carries" for ὁδαίων: the sense is uncertain and the note says so; the paraphrase does not assert more than the note allows.
- 193 `i` "made like a man": ἐικυῖα 'like, made like' is an ordinary rendering and does not claim a transformation.
- 167 `i` "every graceful gift to all men": awkward but the scope of οὐ πάντεσσι is preserved; not changed.
- 167 note "οὕτως points ahead": the word can also point back; not decidable, harmless.
- 111 `l` "the son of Polyneus, Tecton's son": ambiguous in English, but it follows the Greek order and `i` makes the relation explicit.
- Gloss πολυκλήιδι "many-benched, with many thwarts": the dictionary sense; the table's ban on 'many-benched' is for the translation, not the glossary.
- Gloss θαυμανέοντες lemma 'θαυμάζω (epic θαυμαίνω)': cannot be verified without the lexicon in hand; the form and meaning are right; left.
- Gloss μυθεῖαι '(= μυθέεαι, Attic μυθῇ)': acceptable; the note was brought into line instead.
- 104 note "already stands at 2.413": true; 8.46 (odyssey-033) also has it, but the note claims nothing false.
- Remembered English: nothing in `i` matched a modern translation's wording that I could identify; the phrases that come easily ("the equal of Ares", "cowered down", "put your word to him") were checked against the case relations and stand.
- Scansion: none flagged in the packet; nothing hand-scanned; no note added.
